Let me carefully analyze the 7 frames (F0-F6) to determine the 6 events between them.

The apparatus has two rows:
- Upper row: Dipole A (copper/orange electrode on left, blue/green electrode on right)
- Lower row: Dipole B (copper/orange electrode on left, blue/green electrode on right)

Each row has a light probe on the left and a dark probe on the right, sliding horizontally between fixed outer spring anchors.

Wait, let me re-read the apparatus description. "Each row has a light probe on the left and a dark probe on the right, both sliding horizontally between fixed outer spring anchors."

Hmm, but the images show two colored bodies (orange/copper and green/blue) in each row, connected by springs to fixed anchors (gray circles at the ends). Let me look more carefully.

Actually, looking at the images: In each row, there's a gray circle (anchor) on the far left, then a spring, then an orange/copper body, then a gap, then a green/blue body, then a spring, then a gray circle (anchor) on the far right. So the orange body and green body are the two electrodes of the dipole, and they slide between the fixed outer spring anchors (the gray circles).

Wait, but the description says "a light probe on the left and a dark probe on the right". Hmm. Let me reconsider. The "light probe" and "dark probe" might refer to the colored bodies? The orange/copper is the copper electrode, the green/blue is the blue electrode. But the description also says "In each dipole, the copper electrode is on the left and the blue electrode is on the right." So the copper (orange) is left, blue (green) is right.

Then what are the "light probe" and "dark probe"? Maybe the small spheres at the very left and right edges (the brown-ish sphere at far left and blue-ish sphere at far right)? Those look like fixed balls. Hmm.

Actually, re-reading: "The four light probes have charge signs +, -, +, - from upper-left to lower-right." So there are 4 probes total: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right. And "The two upper probes have mass 0.025 kg... the two lower probes have mass 0.550 kg..."

So the probes are the sliding bodies! In each row, there are two probes? No wait, "light probe on the left and dark probe on the right" per row. So upper row has a light probe (left) and dark probe (right). Lower row has light probe (left) and dark probe (right). That's 4 probes. Their charge signs: upper-left=+, upper-right=-, lower-left=+, lower-right=-.

Hmm, but then what about the electrodes? "In each dipole, the copper electrode is on the left and the blue electrode is on the right." So the dipole is the source, with copper (left) and blue (right) electrodes. The probes are separate sliding masses that respond to the dipole's field.

OK so in the image, the orange body = copper electrode (left of dipole), green body = blue electrode (right of dipole). The probes... hmm but I see only two bodies per row (orange and green). Where are the probes?

Wait, maybe I'm misreading the image. Let me look again. In each row I see: gray circle (left anchor), spring, orange body, [gap], green body, spring, gray circle (right anchor). Plus at the very edges there are small spheres (brown at left, blue at right) which might be the outer spring anchors? And the gray circles are... hmm.

Actually the description: "both sliding horizontally between fixed outer spring anchors." So the two bodies (probes?) slide between the fixed outer spring anchors (the small spheres at the very edges). And the springs connect the probes to the anchors.

So in each row, the left body (orange) is the "light probe on the left"? And the right body (green) is the "dark probe on the right"? But then where are the electrodes? The description says copper electrode on left, blue electrode on right. Maybe the orange IS the copper electrode which is also the left probe? This is getting confusing.

Let me step back. The exact physics mapping is probably not critical for the labeling task. What matters is: as charge magnitude of A or B increases, the forces on the probes change, causing displacement. I need to look at the displacement patterns across frames to infer which charge changed.

Let me look at the positions of the bodies across frames. I'll track the horizontal position of the left (orange) body and right (green) body in each row.

Let me define positions by pixel x-coordinate of the center of each body. The image is 1024 wide.

Frame F0:
Upper row: orange body center ~ x=350; green body center ~ x=670.
Lower row: orange body center ~ x=345; green body center ~ x=650.

Frame F1:
Upper: orange ~345; green ~670.
Lower: orange ~330; green ~670.

Frame F2:

Hmm, these are rough. Let me look more carefully at the images. This is hard to do precisely by eye. Let me think about the spring compression/extension as the visual cue. The springs between anchor and body: when a body moves outward (toward anchor), the spring compresses (shorter, denser coils); when body moves inward (toward center), spring stretches.

Actually the displacement of probes is the key observable. Let me think about the physics: A dipole produces a field; the probes (charges) feel forces. If the dipole charge magnitude increases, the force on each probe increases, so the probe equilibrium shifts.

The signs: upper-left probe +, upper-right probe -, lower-left +, lower-right -. The dipole A upper row: copper electrode (left) is + presumably, blue (right) is -. A dipole with + on left, - on right.

For a probe to the left of the dipole (i.e., left of copper +), the + probe would be repelled by + and attracted by -, net... The + electrode is closer, so repulsion dominates → probe pushed left (outward). The - probe to the left would be attracted to + → pulled right (inward). Hmm but both probes are in the same row on opposite sides? Wait, "light probe on the left and dark probe on the right" — left probe is left of the dipole, right probe is right of the dipole.

This is too detailed. The task likely expects a simpler pattern-matching: look at whether probes move apart or together, and which row moved, to decide Increase/Decrease of A or B.

Given the difficulty, perhaps the intended answer is a sequence where each event changes one charge, and the visible motion is in the corresponding row.

F1 → F2: Lower row returns (orange 330→345, green 670→650). So lower moved inward back. That suggests a decrease? But wait F2 should be after event 2. If event1 was IncreaseB (outward at F1), event2 could be DecreaseB (inward at F2). But then F2 lower equals F0 lower. Plausible.

F2 → F3: lower orange 345→330 (outward left), green 650→670 (outward right). Again lower outward. So event3 = IncreaseB? But that contradicts monotonic? Actually charges can be increased multiple times? "A single source control changes A by 25 or B by 50 in indicated direction; the sign does not change." Magnitudes can be increased/decreased repeatedly, presumably within some range. So multiple increases allowed.

This is too uncertain. Let me look at the overall trend more globally.

Let me define "outwardness" per row as the gap between the two bodies (center distance). Larger gap = probes pushed apart = stronger field = larger charge. Smaller gap = weaker.

Interpretation: gap increases when charge magnitude increases (probes pushed apart), gap decreases when charge decreases (probes pulled together toward center).

F5: gaps even smaller → further decrease? But that would be another decrease event. event5 = DecreaseA + DecreaseB? Or maybe the motion is still settling.

Hmm wait, but the protocol says evidence frame is ~3.5s after event, before next. So each frame reflects the new equilibrium (mostly settled) after that event. Persistent motion from earlier shouldn't be counted.

F6: gaps return to ~280 (same as F4). So after F5's small gap, F6 gap increased relative to F5 → increase? event6 = IncreaseA + IncreaseB?

prompt:
Infer exactly 6 hidden events from exactly 7 chronological interior images F0-F6. F0 is the initial evidence frame before the first event. Each subsequent image adds one new event. Use only these supplied images and the public apparatus description. Reconstruct the complete unordered set of controls at every supplied event; events are ordered in time.

APPARATUS AND PUBLIC CONTROL DEFINITIONS
APPARATUS
The fixed camera looks at two horizontal rows; image-right is world +x and image-up is +y. The upper row is Dipole A and the lower row is Dipole B. Each row has a light probe on the left and a dark probe on the right, both sliding horizontally between fixed outer spring anchors. A and B are separate, spatially distinct dipoles. In each dipole, the copper electrode is on the left and the blue electrode is on the right. A small neutral ivory body is fixed between the rows. The dipoles and the neutral body remain part of the apparatus throughout the sequence.

CALIBRATION FACTS FOR THIS APPARATUS
At the start of every sample, the hidden source magnitudes are A=37.5 microC and B=75.0 microC. A single source control changes A by 25.0 microC or B by 50.0 microC in the indicated direction; the sign of each source does not change. The four light probes have charge signs +, -, +, - from upper-left to lower-right. The two upper probes have mass 0.025 kg and spring damping 0.305 N s/m; the two lower probes have mass 0.550 kg and damping 1.20 N s/m. The neutral ivory body has mass 0.120 kg. These values are calibration information about the fixed apparatus, not labels for the hidden events.

ALLOWED LABELS
IncreaseChargeA: increase the magnitude of upper Dipole A while preserving its electrode signs.
DecreaseChargeA: decrease the magnitude of upper Dipole A while preserving its electrode signs.
IncreaseChargeB: increase the magnitude of lower Dipole B while preserving its electrode signs.
DecreaseChargeB: decrease the magnitude of lower Dipole B while preserving its electrode signs.
An event contains one label or one A label together with one B label. Do not add a label merely because a probe is still moving from an earlier event.

OBSERVATION PROTOCOL FOR THIS PREFIX
The evidence frame is taken about 3.5 s after its corresponding event, before the next one. Use fixed anchors, row identity, probe signs, relative displacement and persistent motion; one probe or colour alone does not identify an event.
Capture times (physical/native capture time in seconds): F0=1.966667 s; F1=5.500000 s; F2=11.000000 s; F3=16.500000 s; F4=22.000000 s; F5=27.500000 s; F6=33.000000 s.

ALLOWED ATOMIC LABELS
IncreaseChargeA, DecreaseChargeA, IncreaseChargeB, DecreaseChargeB

ALLOWED EVENT LABEL SETS
[["IncreaseChargeA"],["DecreaseChargeA"],["IncreaseChargeB"],["DecreaseChargeB"],["IncreaseChargeA","IncreaseChargeB"],["DecreaseChargeB","IncreaseChargeA"],["DecreaseChargeA","IncreaseChargeB"],["DecreaseChargeA","DecreaseChargeB"]]

REQUIRED OUTPUT
Return only one valid JSON object with exactly one root field, "operations". Its value must contain exactly 6 nonempty lists, in chronological event order. Every inner list must equal one allowed event label set and comply with the control rules above. Order within an event list does not matter. Even if uncertain, select your best-supported allowed answer for every event. Never return an empty list, null, unknown, abstention, or a missing event. Do not output markdown, commentary, or additional fields.
FINAL ANSWER CONTRACT: Give exactly 6 chronological event arrays under the sole JSON key "operations". Choose the most likely legal answer for EVERY event even when uncertain. Do not abstain, return an empty answer, or omit simultaneous actions. Your final visible answer must be only the JSON object. Legal action sets for one event: [["IncreaseChargeA"], ["DecreaseChargeA"], ["IncreaseChargeB"], ["DecreaseChargeB"], ["IncreaseChargeA", "IncreaseChargeB"], ["DecreaseChargeB", "IncreaseChargeA"], ["DecreaseChargeA", "IncreaseChargeB"], ["DecreaseChargeA", "DecreaseChargeB"]].
title: Electric dipoles

paragraphs: The camera faces horizontal rows of electrical probes. Dipole A occupies the upper row and dipole B the lower. Each dipole has a copper electrode on its left and a blue electrode on its right. Between the fixed outer spring anchors, a positively charged probe slides on the left and a negatively charged probe on the right. A neutral ivory body sits between the rows and provides a stationary point of reference.

The lower source starts with a larger charge magnitude and its control changes that magnitude by a larger increment than the upper control. In either row the electrodes keep their signs. Changing a source changes the forces on its spring-mounted probes. Compare the separation and displacement of the probes against the anchors in successive images. The probes in the lower row are heavier and respond more slowly; a position seen after a command can therefore reflect motion inherited from an earlier event.

Identify any change in the upper source, IncreaseChargeA or DecreaseChargeA, and any change in the lower source, IncreaseChargeB or DecreaseChargeB. A command may change a source by itself or change both sources simultaneously. Each selected dipole takes a single direction of change. Return all selected labels for each event in chronological order under the sole JSON key “operations”.
